questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has $AB = 5\text{ cm}$, $BC = 7\text{ cm}$, and $\angle B = 60°$. Triangle $DEF$ has $DE = 5\text{ cm}$, $EF = 7\text{ cm}$, and $\angle E = 60°$. Which congruence condition applies?
questions.explanation: Two sides and the included angle are known in each triangle: $AB = DE$, $BC = EF$, and the angle between them $\angle B = \angle E = 60°$. This is the SAS condition.

questions.stem: Two right-angled triangles have equal hypotenuses and one other pair of equal sides. Which congruence condition proves they are congruent?
questions.explanation: RHS (Right angle, Hypotenuse, Side) is the congruence condition specifically for right-angled triangles where the hypotenuse and one other side are equal.

questions.stem: Why is AAA not a valid congruence condition?

options.text: Because it only works for right-angled triangles
Because two triangles can have the same angles but different sizes
Because you need at least four pieces of information
Because angles in a triangle always sum to $180°$ so the third angle is redundant

questions.explanation: AAA proves that two triangles are similar (same shape) but not necessarily congruent (same size). Triangles with the same angles can be different sizes -- they are enlargements of each other.
